summary: Port Hueneme is one of only two cities in Ventura County with its own deepwater harbor — a working commercial port that also hosts Naval Base Ventura County, the area's dominant employer and the reason this tiny 4.7-square-mile city exists in its current form. That military and logistics backbone means this is genuinely a job center, not a bedroom community, though the defense-heavy economy limits employer variety; switching jobs without a longer commute toward Oxnard, Camarillo, or the 101 corridor is difficult outside the public sector. The coastal setting delivers year-round mildness — average highs around 70°F with 9.1 hours of daily sunshine and nighttime lows rarely dipping below 55°F — and the beach at Hueneme Beach Park offers unobstructed Pacific sunsets without the crowds of Ventura or Santa Barbara. At a median home value of $556,200 against a median household income of $76,655, the price-to-income ratio sits above 7:1, making buying a genuine stretch at the median; rents averaging $2,106 consume roughly a third of that same gross income. The street grid is flat and compact enough that errands can be managed without a car in spots, but the city is bisected by the naval base and port infrastructure, which fragments connectivity and limits the walkable fabric to a few residential blocks near the waterfront. Port Hueneme is essentially a small military-adjacent beach town with big-county housing costs and a quieter commercial strip than its neighbors — affordable by Ventura County standards, but shaped more by the base's rhythms than by any independent downtown energy.
